note: Measured on the file-backed host engine AFTER the circular allocator landed but BEFORE the futile-reclaim guard. The workload writes 8000 distinct keys into a 1 MiB region whose log area is 10 segments x 32768 B = 320 KiB, so the live set is ~2.8x what the region can hold. The engine accepted every write instead of reporting FlashFull, sustaining itself by relocating live data indefinitely.
diagnosis: Live set exceeds log capacity (u = 2.83). Theorem 19's WA_gc = 1/(1-u) does not apply above u = 1; the correct response is FlashFull. Guard added: refuse compaction once a completed pass relocates more than GC_FUTILE_RELOCATION_PCT (97%) of the records it scanned.
